newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH MONEY MARKET RATES UNMOVED, AWAIT U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH MONEY MARKET RATES UNMOVED, AWAIT U.S. DATA.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were little changed on Tuesday as traders awaited fresh economic data, mainly from the United States, to help determine direction.
Dealers said Wednesday's U.S. retail sales report was a key figure for the market.
A Reuters survey of economists sees July sales up 0.7 percent compared to up 0.5 percent in June. Ex-autos, sales are seen up 0.5 percent.
"A stronger figure could trigger inflation worries," said one dealer, adding this would probably press rates higher.
July producer prices are also due on Wednesday. The overall and core rates were each expected to gain 0.1 percent.
Another dealer said he was also watching the dollar.
The dollar was trading at 2.0978 guilders by 1210 GMT versus just above 2.10 guilders in early trade.
"Such a small move will not have any impact on the money market. But rates are likely to rise if the dollar gains further," the dealer said.
Call money rates were bid at an unchanged 3.18 percent and three-month deposits were stable at 3.34 percent bid.
The guilder was trading at 112.66 per 100 marks, unchanged from the previous day.
